title: Transdermal Implants: Body Art or Nightmare Fuel?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explore transdermal implants, an extreme body modification in which an anchor sits under the skin with a post protruding through it, and contrast them with subdermal implants (fully under the skin), magnet finger implants and grinder/bio-hacking culture, microdermals, and genital piercings. They cover the mod father Steve Haworth and his dermal elevator, the risks of infection, rejection and nerve damage, the legal question of whether the procedure counts as surgery, and the life of Dennis Avner (Stalking Cat). The episode opens with tour and schedule banter and ends with listener mail about google sculpting and flarf poetry.

segments.title: Opening banter and tour schedule
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about the year's last full-length recording, upcoming live shows in Seattle, Los Angeles, Sketchfest and Portland, and a Movie Crush show, before introducing the topic.

segments.title: Body modification and subdermal implants overview
segments.summary: They frame body modification as a broad umbrella including piercing, tattooing and gauging, discuss motivations such as self-expression and tribal affiliation, and introduce subdermal implants like skull shapes, which can be lit, versus transdermal ones.

segments.title: Genital beading and magnet finger implants
segments.summary: They describe genital beading for sexual enhancement, then discuss magnetic fingertip implants for sensory augmentation, George Dvorsky's article, and a Wired writer whose magnet reassembled after a failed removal.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break; hosts joke about magnets and MRI risks before the break.

segments.title: Transdermal implants defined and mod father Steve Haworth
segments.summary: Transdermal implants are defined as implants that break the skin envelope, distinguished from subdermal ones. Steve Haworth, a medical tool engineer, is described as the mod father who designed tools, procedures and implants.

segments.title: Dennis Avner, Stalking Cat
segments.summary: Dennis Avner, known as Stalking Cat, a Navy veteran, underwent facial surgery, tooth filing, dentures and tattoos to resemble a tiger. He died by suicide before reaching his goal, and the hosts note he is considered an outlier with possible mental health issues.

segments.title: Anchors, legality and the implant procedure
segments.summary: Anchors are clover or figure-eight shaped with gaps for scar tissue to grow through. The hosts discuss whether the procedure counts as surgery in legal terms, then walk through the step-by-step procedure with incisions, a dermal elevator and an implant pushed through the pocket.

segments.title: Risks: infection, rejection, nerve damage
segments.summary: Risks include skull infection and abscess, rejection, migration, and the danger of butter knives or going too deep. Hosts share personal injury anecdotes, and microdermals are introduced as a smaller, safer alternative with easier removal.

segments.title: Genital piercings list
segments.summary: The hosts list adult genital piercings for men and women, with a caution about content and some names such as Guiches and Prince's Wand, and point listeners to a How Stuff Works article on body modification.

segments.title: Listener mail: google sculpting and flarf
segments.summary: A listener explains that flarf poetry uses Google sculpting to build poems from search results, and shares an example poem.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to get in touch via the website and email.
